nodes.label: Implementation Checklist for the Coding Agent
nodes.norm_label: implementation checklist for the coding agent

nodes.label: Batch-Tool Preference by Schema Removal
nodes.rationale: The old prompt merely stated a batch-tool preference and the model ignored it, so redundant single-action tools are removed from the offered tools array; a tool the model cannot see cannot be picked.

nodes.label: Strict JSON Schema Data Contracts
nodes.rationale: Every LLM response is machine-checked before another line of the harness runs, with reject-and-retry once then escalate; this is what removes ambiguity as a category of bug.

nodes.label: Failure: Plan Can Silently Lose the Original Goal
nodes.norm_label: failure: plan can silently lose the original goal
nodes.rationale: Replans splice in new subtasks without re-queueing the original goal subtask, so the run ended with decision=continue and an empty remaining_plan having never navigated to YouTube; no invariant forbade the plan from emptying out.

nodes.label: Principle: Determinism Before Reasoning
nodes.rationale: Anything with a fixed, checkable answer is handled by code; the LLM is reserved for intent, tool selection under ambiguity, and success/failure interpretation.

nodes.label: Principle: Escalate to the LLM Only on Genuine Deviation
nodes.norm_label: principle: escalate to the llm only on genuine deviation
nodes.rationale: Expected, scriptable failures (browser not running, tab not found, element not yet rendered) go through deterministic retry/bootstrap first; the LLM sees them only if deterministic recovery also fails.

nodes.label: Principle: The Goal Is a First-Class Object That Cannot Be Dropped
nodes.norm_label: principle: the goal is a first-class object that cannot be dropped
nodes.rationale: The original goal and success condition live outside the mutable subtask queue in session state for the whole run, so no replan, recovery, or infra fix-up may complete a run without re-checking that success condition.

nodes.label: Prompts Are a Second Line of Defense
nodes.norm_label: prompts are a second line of defense
nodes.rationale: An LLM instruction is a strong bias, not a hard constraint, so schema/tool availability, runtime-side validation and the destructive-action gate must be enforced in code regardless of the prompt.

nodes.label: Guards Fixture: Occlusion and Node-Replacement Probes
nodes.norm_label: guards fixture: occlusion and node-replacement probes

nodes.label: P1.1 Follow-ups (scroll chaining, settle tuning, Laya heads, Enter discipline)
nodes.norm_label: p1.1 follow-ups (scroll chaining, settle tuning, laya heads, enter discipline)

nodes.label: Delegated Click Handler for Cloned Nodes
nodes.norm_label: delegated click handler for cloned nodes
nodes.rationale: The click handler is delegated on document so cloned/replaced nodes retain behavior, which is what makes the detached-node identity guard meaningful.

nodes.label: P0 Gap: Scroll Dropped in observed()
nodes.norm_label: p0 gap: scroll dropped in observed()
nodes.rationale: browser_policy.rs observed() filters to click/fill/select, so scroll never reaches the policy and below-fold targets are unreachable; the feed bench failing with max_steps is the proof.

nodes.label: P0 Gap: Typing Always Sends Enter
nodes.norm_label: p0 gap: typing always sends enter
nodes.rationale: fill does selectAll then insertText then Enter unconditionally, which hides combobox suggestions; making Enter conditional is required rather than worked around in probes.

nodes.label: P0 Gap: wait_for_load Burns Full Polls
nodes.norm_label: p0 gap: wait_for_load burns full polls
nodes.rationale: 300ms double-stable (text,inter,href) polling up to 20s burns roughly 60 polls on streaming SPAs even though the timeout is best-effort, so CDP cost is dominated by waiting rather than snapshots.

nodes.label: --force-renderer-accessibility Gotcha
nodes.rationale: Brave's AT-SPI tree is empty without --force-renderer-accessibility, and because Brave is single-instance, --new-window on a running process inherits the missing flag; CDP AX via Stagehand works without it and is therefore preferred for browsers.

nodes.label: Search Fixture: SPA with Stale Node IDs
nodes.norm_label: search fixture: spa with stale node ids

nodes.label: Suggestion Re-Render on Every Keystroke
nodes.rationale: Suggestion nodes are replaced on every keystroke and the results list is fully re-rendered, deliberately producing the stale-ID SPA shape that picker scanning and WeakMap identity must survive.

nodes.label: P0 Gap: No Anti-Thrash or DONE Verifier
nodes.norm_label: p0 gap: no anti-thrash or done verifier
nodes.rationale: run_browser_loop had no 3x-no-change blocked check and no independent verification of open/finish before reporting Done, so a thrashing loop looked like success.

nodes.label: P0 Gap: Per-Step Laya Fan-Out
nodes.rationale: pick_element fans out to up to five evaluate_choice_batch chunks per step, so Laya was not fused (10 predicts for 10 steps); P1 collapses it to one speculative forward pass per fan-out.

nodes.label: Safety Rules (confirm before send, re-verify desktop, prefer address: selector)
nodes.norm_label: safety rules (confirm before send, re-verify desktop, prefer address: selector)

nodes.label: Destructive-Action Runtime Gate
nodes.rationale: Deletion, sending, purchasing and irreversible settings must require explicit confirmation via a runtime gate keyed off the capability index destructive flag, not something the model has to remember to apply.

nodes.label: Open X Never Means Launch a Second Window
nodes.norm_label: open x never means launch a second window
nodes.rationale: If a usable browser context already exists, browser_open is removed from the offered tool list for that call; removing the footgun from the schema is stronger than asking the model not to pick it.

nodes.label: Stagehand to Eval to Snapshot to Screenshot Priority (0.6)
nodes.norm_label: stagehand to eval to snapshot to screenshot priority (0.6)
nodes.rationale: CDP eval is fast but Stagehand handles AX mapping, twoStep dropdowns, self-heal and ref invalidation robustly, so Stagehand goes first and screenshots are verify-only (~50ms per key versus a 2-4s vision loop).

nodes.label: State-Aware Resume and Tab Deduplication
nodes.rationale: Before navigating, an existing page tab with the same host/query is reused via /json/activate and location.href is verified, because restarting from step 1 or opening a second tab wastes work and browser_snapshot alone is unreliable with multiple tabs.

nodes.label: Provider-Native tools Parameter and tool_calls Array
nodes.norm_label: provider-native tools parameter and tool_calls array

nodes.label: Merging Router + Planner for Simple Tasks
nodes.norm_label: merging router + planner for simple tasks

nodes.label: Call-Count Instrumentation Metric
nodes.rationale: Instrumenting call count per task from day one and alerting above the budget is what keeps the system honest as it grows past the YouTube example.

nodes.label: Failure: No Native Tool Calling
nodes.rationale: Pasting tool descriptions into the user message and parsing hand-rolled JSON blocks the model from expressing multi-step tool sequences, requires brittle bespoke parsing, and forfeits native parallel tool calls.

nodes.label: Principle: One Call Plans, Many Tools Execute
nodes.norm_label: principle: one call plans, many tools execute
nodes.rationale: Planning and execution are different concerns and must not be interleaved into one-tool-call-one-round-trip: the LLM decides the sequence, the runtime executes it without returning to the LLM unless it deviates.

nodes.label: Fixed goal_statement + success_condition Contract
nodes.rationale: The goal and success condition are written once by the router and passed unchanged to the next call and any recovery, so downstream steps cannot silently redefine what done means.

nodes.label: Tool-Naming Split (names tools, not steps or arguments)
nodes.norm_label: tool-naming split (names tools, not steps or arguments)
nodes.rationale: The router names the smallest sufficient tool set from a one-line-description catalog; argument and ordering decisions wait for the call that has the full schema for those specific tools.

nodes.label: Grounding in the Request's Own Words
nodes.norm_label: grounding in the request's own words
nodes.rationale: Subtasks may reuse the request's own titles, sites and file names but must never invent app names, URLs, credentials, UI labels, or extra login/payment/install steps the user did not ask for.

nodes.label: No Invented UI State Rule
nodes.rationale: The model is explicitly instructed not to invent UI state, IDs, coordinates, tab numbers or arguments unsupported by supplied context, so observation precedes action.

nodes.label: One Reasoning Model + Deterministic Rust Runtime
nodes.norm_label: one reasoning model + deterministic rust runtime
nodes.rationale: There is no secondary or cheap model in the execution path: the main model owns strategy, decomposition, tool selection, verification and recovery, while the runtime supplies exact tool schemas, validates tool and arguments, enforces approvals and execution budgets, and records live evidence.

nodes.label: lucy-tools (native tool registry and built-in tools)
nodes.norm_label: lucy-tools (native tool registry and built-in tools)

nodes.label: Shell Dangerous-Command Guard (LUCY_ALLOW_DANGEROUS)
nodes.rationale: rm -rf /, mkfs, dd if=, fork bombs and shutdown/reboot/poweroff are blocked unless LUCY_ALLOW_DANGEROUS=1, with a 120s timeout and 64KB output cap, because shell is the only tool with environment-level blast radius.

nodes.label: ADK-Rust Optional Capability Layer
nodes.rationale: ADK-Rust is consumed as a library for complementary capabilities (memory, workflow/graph primitives, artifacts, skills, plugins, sandbox, evaluation, telemetry, auth) and deliberately does not replace Lucy's latency-sensitive execution engine.

nodes.label: Non-Vendoring and MIT Notice Preservation Policy
nodes.norm_label: non-vendoring and mit notice preservation policy
nodes.rationale: Upstream code is re-implemented rather than vendored, but the MIT notice and pinned LICENSE blob e921bccf are retained because Lucy's design work materially draws from those upstream modules.

nodes.label: Workspace Cargo Check + Test Gate
nodes.rationale: A single cargo check + cargo test --workspace pair gates pushes to main and all PRs; a cheap whole-workspace compile/test gate is chosen over lint-heavy CI to keep the feedback loop short.

nodes.label: lucy-core (shared domain types, tool/model interfaces, cancellation)
nodes.norm_label: lucy-core (shared domain types, tool/model interfaces, cancellation)

nodes.label: lucy-mcp (MCP config and persistent stdio transport)
nodes.norm_label: lucy-mcp (mcp config and persistent stdio transport)

nodes.label: Modular Workspace Architecture
nodes.rationale: The architecture is modular so the UI, agent loop, tools, MCP integration, memory, and model providers can evolve independently.

nodes.label: Harness Architecture v2: Minimal-Call, Zero-Ambiguity Design
nodes.community_name: v1 vs v2 Harness Trace Analysis
nodes.norm_label: harness architecture v2: minimal-call, zero-ambiguity design

nodes.label: Failure: Environment Bootstrapping Routed Through Reasoning Model
nodes.community_name: v1 vs v2 Harness Trace Analysis
nodes.norm_label: failure: environment bootstrapping routed through reasoning model
nodes.rationale: Whether the browser runs with --remote-debugging-port is deterministic and checkable in milliseconds, yet 8 of 13 LLM calls were spent guessing binary names and racing the port; this needed a state machine, not judgment.

nodes.label: Failure: One LLM Call Per Action Plus Per Verification
nodes.community_name: v1 vs v2 Harness Trace Analysis
nodes.norm_label: failure: one llm call per action plus per verification
nodes.rationale: A dedicated Tool Selector per subtask plus a Closed-Loop Controller after every result turns a single click into three LLM round-trips before any task progress is made.

nodes.label: Principle: Verify the Outcome, Not the Step
nodes.community_name: v1 vs v2 Harness Trace Analysis
nodes.norm_label: principle: verify the outcome, not the step
nodes.rationale: success:true or HTTP 200 is not evidence of task success, so verification happens once per plan against the user's success condition rather than after every individual tool call.

nodes.label: 250-Action Cap and Below-Fold Scroll Stress
nodes.rationale: Grid density is tuned so more than 250 buttons sit in the 1280x800 viewport at once, which triggers snapshot's 250-action splice plus omitted_actions and proves the below-fold policy bug.

nodes.label: WhatsApp Fullscreen Window Rule
nodes.rationale: A tiled WhatsApp window in Brave traps focus in the omnibox overlay so ctrl+alt+/ and typing get stuck; the window is moved to an empty workspace and fullscreened before any keyboard flow.
